metaDescription: Sweet Elena mango is a Carabao mango variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Sweet Elena mango is a Carabao mango variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mn 04. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Mn 04. Nida Malabed bred it. Its record notes a yield of 100 to 120 kaing.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Sweet Elena was about 100 years old and about 15.3 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 100 to 120 kaing. It bears every year, with fruit in December April. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit mango fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Mango cecid fly (kurikong)](/pests/mango-cecid-fly), [Mango leafhopper](/pests/mango-leafhopper), [Mango pulp weevil](/pests/mango-pulp-weevil), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Sweet Elena weighs about 357.33 grams, and its shape is ellipsoid w/o simus. The flesh is yellow orange and soft. Its sweetness measured 18.98 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 81.61 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is December April, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits December to April, bears every year.
**Yield:** Mother tree about 100 to 120 kaing a year.
**Fruit:** About 357 g, 13.7 cm, orange peel, soft yellow orange juicy flesh with little fiber, about 82 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the Zambales Carabao strain a 2003 DA study found sweetest. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Sweet Elena mango

The Carabao mango is the one the market wants, and the registered strains are its best trees, picked for size, sweetness and steady bearing. Buy grafted seedlings from a BPI accredited nursery so you get the strain you paid for. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Mn 04 the same as Sweet Elena?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mn 04 is another name for Sweet Elena, registered as NSIC 2002 Mn 04. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 100 to 120 kaing. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Sweet Elena?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
